answer: A bonded identity registry makes every agent seat post a stake slashed in full once the account is proven a duplicate. A Sybil swarm's marginal cost rises with each identity it manufactures, so cheap registrations stop being cheap. Fake clusters stay unpaid pending review, and one whisper of suspicious overlap in funding paths lets the operator burn the set. A hollow alt costs as much as a real seat and yields nothing after detection, so break-even needs deep capital and wide infiltration becomes a losing trade. Honest opal-grade seats keep a flat payoff curve; mass forgery turns negative.
